name: jadx - Dex to Java Decompiler
description: jadx decompiles Android Dalvik bytecode (APK/DEX/AAR) back to readable Java source with a GUI (jadx-gui) for navigation, search, and xrefs. The fastest way to understand an app's logic, find hardcoded secrets/URLs, locate auth and crypto, and map exported components.
notes:
=== CLI ===
  jadx <file>                      # decompile APK/DEX -> ./<name>/sources + resources
  jadx -d out <file>               # output dir
  jadx-gui <file>                  # interactive GUI (search, xrefs, deobf)

=== HUNT IN jadx-gui ===
  - Full-text search (Navigation > Text search): "password", "http", "secret", "token", "AES"
  - Resources > AndroidManifest.xml: exported activities/services/receivers, deep links
  - Resources > res/values/strings.xml: API keys, URLs
  - Right-click > Find Usage for sinks (openConnection, getSharedPreferences)

=== DEOBFUSCATE ===
  jadx --deobf <file>              # rename obfuscated identifiers consistently

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  apktool        # smali + resources (for patching)
  bytecode-viewer / Ghidra
  MobSF          # automated pipeline bundling jadx

recommended.note: apktool when you need smali to patch and rebuild.
Confirm findings dynamically with Frida hooks.

defense.why_it_works: Dalvik bytecode retains type and method structure, so decompilers reconstruct readable Java. Any logic or secret shipped in the app is recoverable without running it.
defense.impact: Full understanding of client logic, discovery of hardcoded secrets/endpoints, and identification of weak client-side security controls.
defense.detection: Not detectable (offline decompilation of a distributed app).
defense.prevention: Obfuscation (R8/ProGuard/DexGuard); remove secrets from the client; server-side enforcement of all security logic; string encryption and native code for sensitive routines; integrity attestation.
